Unauthorized Charging Station Registration [Spoofing, Repudiation, CWE-287] on EV Charging Station, OCPP Handler (Fargate), IoT Core, DynamoDB (Telemetry Store): Attackers could create fake charging station identities by exploiting weak device registration processes or by cloning legitimate station credentials. An attacker creates multiple simulated charging stations using stolen or guessed credentials, flooding the system with fake telemetry data and potentially causing resource exhaustion.

Insecure Administrative Access [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-284] on Admin API (API Gateway), DynamoDB (Telemetry Store), S3 (Data Lake), Lambda Functions: The Admin API relies primarily on IP-based restrictions and lacks robust authentication mechanisms. IP spoofing or VPN usage could bypass these controls. An attacker could use a compromised system within the allowed IP range to access the Admin API and manipulate charging station configurations or access sensitive data.

DNS Hijacking Attack [Spoofing, Tampering, CWE-350] on Route53 DNS, Network Load Balancer, EV Charging Station: Attackers could compromise DNS infrastructure, exploit DNSSEC vulnerabilities, or perform cache poisoning attacks to redirect charging station traffic to malicious servers. An attacker performs a DNS cache poisoning attack on the local DNS resolver used by charging stations, redirecting their connections to a malicious server that captures authentication credentials and charging data.

Telemetry Data Tampering [Tampering, Repudiation, CWE-345] on EV Charging Station, IoT Core, DynamoDB (Telemetry Store), S3 (Data Lake): Attackers could intercept and modify telemetry data during transmission, or directly manipulate stored data through compromised credentials or system vulnerabilities. An attacker modifies charging usage data to reduce billing amounts or manipulates power consumption metrics to hide electricity theft.
